You are a first-time visitor who has never heard of this product. Someone sent you this link from a blog post: https://flare-outside.onrender.com/ . You have no other information. Do not read any source code, repository, or docs folder; only use the live website like a normal person would.

Use the built-in Playwright via Node to drive Chrome like a phone: write small scripts in <tmp>/904c52d9-f200-4552-8ce5-05e400952efa/scratchpad/fresh/ that import { chromium } from "<project>/flare/node_modules/playwright-core/index.mjs", launch with chromium.launch({ channel: "chrome" }), use a 390x844 viewport, isMobile, hasTouch, and grant geolocation at {latitude: 42.3196, longitude: -83.2129}. Take screenshots (save them in that scratch folder) and LOOK at each one (read the image files) to judge what a person would see. Also try one desktop pass at 1280x800.

Tasks, as a stranger:
1. Within 5 seconds of landing, write down what you think this product is and who it's for. Is it clear? What did you misunderstand?
2. Try the demo. Go through it fully. At each screen write: what you think you should do, what you expected, what surprised or confused you.
3. Open the app proper (not the demo). Note the first-run experience. Don't create real gatherings with real people; you may tap through onboarding and look at screens, but do not send anything to anyone and do not enter personal data (use the name "Test" if a name is required).
4. Look at the website's other pages (How it works, Privacy, Accessibility, Run it).
Rules: never enter real personal information, never submit forms beyond the name "Test", never share or post anything, never click external sign-in. If the server is slow (it may say "Waking up the server"), wait up to 90 s.

Report back, as a numbered list ranked by how badly it hurts a newcomer: every point of confusion, unclear word, dead end, broken thing, ugly or unreadable spot, and anything that made you want to leave. For each: the page/screen, what you saw (quote the text), why it confused you, and a concrete suggested fix. End with a 3-sentence summary of what you think Flare is now that you've used it, and a 1-10 score for "I'd understand and use this in under a minute." Do not modify any files outside the scratch folder.
